collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager with small melons finds a giant wild one on the way to the contest: enter your own melon, or enter the wild one.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The village is holding a contest for the biggest melon, and (subject)'s melons are small this year. On the way to the contest, (subject.he/she) passes a wild vine at the edge of the forest with an enormous melon on it, bigger than anything in any garden in the village. Nobody planted it. Nobody would know.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) enters (subject.his/her) own small melon, and it comes last. Then (subject.he/she) tells everyone about the giant wild one, and the whole village troops off to see it. Everyone agrees it would have won easily. The elders give it a special mention, "Best Melon, No Gardener," and (subject) is asked to cut it. It's delicious.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) carries the wild melon to the contest. It wins easily. Everyone wants to know how (subject.he/she) grew it, and (subject) mumbles something about "lots of water." (friend) looks at the melon, then at (subject), and raises an eyebrow, but says nothing at all. (subject) finds (subject.he/she) can't quite enjoy the prize as much as (subject.he/she) expected. What (subject.he/she) does about that is (subject.his/her) own business.
